newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian second-tier shares firm, blue chips steady.
newsitem.headline: Russian second-tier shares firm, blue chips steady.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were barely changed in early trading on Tuesday as investors hunted for second-tier stocks, dealers said.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 leading shares opened at 330.38, unchanged from Monday's close.

At 1100 GMT national power company UES EESR.RTS was $0.2255, unchanged from Monday's close, regional utility Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS was $0.260 after $0.261 and LUKoil LKOH.RTS was $14.55 after $14.54.

"We've got used to sharp moves for any reason. Now we must also get used to the fact that the market is gradually growing by two or three percent now that it is broadening and money coming in is going to a large number of shares and not just a few blue chips," said Sergei Kosynkin, head of the trading department at Bank Menatep.
IK Aton trader Boris Shvedsky said there was steady demand from Russian and foreign investors for second-tier stocks.
"Besides the fairly low prices, this interest is due to people building up positions ahead of shareholders' meetings," he said.
At 1100 oil company Tomskneft TOMG.RTS was $9.70 after $9.12 and regional utility Lenenergo LSNG.RTS was $0.995 after $0.945.

Traders said the current equilibrium would persist for a few days on moderate volumes, as most foreign investors wait for Thursday's summit meeting between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin and a possible credit tightening at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
